text.arabic_uthmani: لِّيُدْخِلَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ جَنَّٰتٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا وَيُكَفِّرَ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمْ ۚ وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًۭا

words.gloss_range: purpose particle governing the following subjunctive; not possession or simple direction here
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) makes the ayah open as purpose rather than as a detached reward description. The small bound particle carries the preceding opening and inner stabilization into their named outcome: admission, expiation, and then divine valuation. Because it governs the following subjunctive, the first sound of the ayah already tells the reader that the garden scene is teleological.

topics.headline: purpose chain continues
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 48:5 as the purpose of the preceding opening and inner stabilization, not as a new isolated scene.
topics.reason: The bundle identifies the particle as purpose lām governing a subjunctive verb, and the boundary rows explicitly connect 48:4 to the outcome named in 48:5.

topics.headline: bound particle launches the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a one-letter prefix fixes the semantic frame before any garden image appears.
topics.reason: The following subjunctive selects purpose, while the bound position makes the dependency visible and audible at the ayah opening.

words.gloss_range: caused admission into a bounded reward domain under the purpose clause
words.root_gloss_range: entry, crossing into an inside, and related innerness or hidden-defect branches; the local Form IV selects caused admission while letting boundary-crossing remain vivid
words.prose: {{ar:يُدْخِلَ}} ({{tr:yudkhila}}) is a purpose-governed causative verb: the believers do not merely enter, they are caused to cross into the reward domain by the implicit divine agent. The root keeps the scene spatial and thresholded, while the Form IV shape puts decisive agency with God. The same verb also starts the paired purpose structure, so admission is heard together with the later removal of misdeeds rather than as a stand-alone prize.

topics.headline: subjunctive under purpose
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that admission is grammatically tied to the preceding purpose frame and paired with expiation under the same aim.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verb subjunctive under purpose lām, and the attachment evidence coordinates it with the later subjunctive verb.

topics.headline: divine caused entry
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the reward as divine admission, with God causing the movement rather than the believers simply entering by themselves.
topics.reason: The Form IV analysis and local valency license a causative admission event with an implicit divine subject, explicit believer objects, and garden destination.

topics.headline: threshold crossing image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the garden promise as an actual boundary crossing into an inside, while hidden-defect associations remain secondary to the local admission sense.
topics.reason: The local form selects caused entry; broader innerness and defect branches can enrich the admission-and-expiation pairing but do not replace the entry sense.

topics.headline: paradise-entry formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the local admission as part of a wider Quranic paradise-entry pattern, including recurrence in 48:17, 48:25, and 48:27.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence and surah-local rows support a formulaic entry field, while the phonetic row adds local texture without changing the sense.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine plural active participle naming the recognized believing group as object of admission
words.root_gloss_range: belief, trust, safety, and granting security; the local participle names an ongoing believing/security identity
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ}} ({{tr:al-mu'minina}}) names a definite, already recognized believing group as the first object of divine admission. Its active-participle form keeps belief as an ongoing identity, and the root's safety field makes the people being admitted those already marked by trust and security. The masculine plural also prepares for the explicit feminine partner, so the object field is about to widen rather than remain absorbed in a generic collective.

topics.headline: recognized object of admission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the admitted people are the known believing community and are grammatically recipients of divine action.
topics.reason: The noun is definite accusative and is attached as the first direct object of the admission verb.

topics.headline: ongoing trust identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees belief as a sustained trust-and-security identity rather than a one-time past act.
topics.reason: The active participle and root-family evidence support an ongoing believing identity colored by trust and safety.

topics.headline: same community carried forward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same believers from inward stabilization in 48:4 to bodily admission in 48:5.
topics.reason: Contextual and boundary rows identify the same believing group across the verse boundary.

topics.headline: paradise formula and gender setup
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this masculine plural as the first half of a gender-paired paradise formula that also recurs in 48:17.
topics.reason: The following conjoined feminine plural and co-occurrence evidence place the word inside a recognized believer-and-garden-entry pattern.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction joining the feminine believer noun to the same object chain
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is small, but it decides the structure: the following feminine plural is coordinated with the masculine plural under the same admission verb. The particle keeps one divine action while widening the object field, and the surah-local comparison lets that paired community also anticipate later admission language in 48:27.

topics.headline: coordinated gender pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that believing women are attached to the same act of admission, not appended as an afterthought.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the two believer nouns as parallel object groups under the same governing verb.

topics.headline: later communal entry anticipation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect this gender-paired admission promise with the later communal entry motif in 48:27.
topics.reason: The contextual rows link the local paired object field with the surah's later entry motif without making that later scene control the local grammar.

words.gloss_range: definite feminine plural active participle conjoined as a full parallel object of admission
words.root_gloss_range: belief, trust, safety, and granting security; the local feminine participle carries the same continuing iman identity as the masculine plural
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ}} ({{tr:al-mu'minati}}) makes the feminine believer group explicit inside the same accusative object chain. The grammar does not let the women disappear into an assumed generic masculine: definiteness, case, and active-participle form match the preceding noun, so the same trust-and-security identity and the same divine admission apply in parallel. The paired expression also belongs to recognizable paradise formulae such as 9:72 and 57:12.

topics.headline: full feminine object parallel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees believing women explicitly included as full parallel recipients of divine admission.
topics.reason: The feminine plural is accusative, definite, and conjoined to the masculine object, matching its syntactic role.

topics.headline: same continuing iman state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the feminine plural bears the same ongoing trust-and-security identity, not a reduced label.
topics.reason: The active-participle form and root evidence apply equally to the feminine plural in the local phrase.

topics.headline: recognized believer-pair formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the gendered pair as a Quranic paradise formula, with parallels in 9:72 and 57:12 and a contrastive setup for 48:6.
topics.reason: The contextual rows give concrete formulaic parallels and a near passage contrast without altering the local parse.

topics.headline: collective widened at boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the prior collective believer reference from 48:4 as it becomes explicitly gender-paired in 48:5.
topics.reason: Boundary evidence identifies a shift from prior collective reference to explicit gender-paired object set.

words.gloss_range: indefinite plural garden destination of admission, expansive rather than a single named location
words.root_gloss_range: covering, concealment, shelter, and garden as enclosed life; the local noun selects garden-realms while preserving protective enclosure
words.prose: {{ar:جَنَّٰتٍۢ}} ({{tr:jannatin}}) is not a single named site but an indefinite plural destination governed by the admission verb. The form makes the reward expansive and distributive: multiple enclosed garden-realms can be entered and inhabited. The root's concealment field gives the gardens protective shelter, and that covering image later meets the different covering of misdeeds, so paradise is both located landscape and sheltered life.

topics.headline: expansive plural destination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the destination as expansive plural garden-realms, not a narrowly identified single place.
topics.reason: The noun is an indefinite plural object complement governed by the admission verb.

topics.headline: garden as sheltered enclosure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the gardens as protective enclosed spaces, while the local noun still means gardens rather than every branch of concealment.
topics.reason: The root family licenses shelter and concealment imagery, but the local concrete noun and syntax select the garden destination.

topics.headline: river-beneath formula landscape
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the gardens as the anchor of a stable river-beneath paradise scene rather than decorative scenery.
topics.reason: The following modifier and co-occurrence rows place the plural garden noun in the recurrent garden-river-beneath formula.

topics.headline: concealment and expiation echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices two different coverings in the ayah: sheltered garden enclosure and the later covering-away of misdeeds.
topics.reason: The rows compare concealment in the garden root with the later covering root as a local semantic contrast.

words.gloss_range: ongoing flowing motion in the garden description, indicative rather than purpose-subjunctive
words.root_gloss_range: running, flowing, and unfolding movement; the local sense is water-like continuous flow, not every transitive or eventive branch
words.prose: {{ar:تَجْرِى}} ({{tr:tajri}}) turns the garden destination into an active scene: the rivers are flowing as an ongoing fact. Its indicative imperfect is not governed like the two purpose verbs, so it describes the gardens rather than adding another purpose action. The feminine singular agreement with a nonhuman plural subject and the stable formulaic flow phrase both make the landscape feel conventional and alive.

topics.headline: ongoing descriptive flow
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the flowing is a standing garden description, not a third subjunctive purpose act.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verb as indicative imperfect modifying the garden noun, not as another verb governed by the purpose particle.

topics.headline: feminine singular agreement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the feminine singular verb is grammatically normal for the nonhuman plural river subject.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the explicit river noun as subject, while the grammar row explains the feminine singular agreement.

topics.headline: continuous water motion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels continuous water motion in the garden scene, while broader event-unfolding uses stay secondary.
topics.reason: The local subject is rivers and the prepositional source phrase selects concrete flowing, with broader flow imagery only enriching the scene.

topics.headline: stable paradise-flow formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the flow phrase as a stable paradise formula, including the recurrence in 48:17.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence and surah-local rows show the same paradise-flow pattern returning later in the surah.

words.gloss_range: source preposition selecting origin beneath the gardens, not a partitive reading here
words.prose: {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) makes the river motion originate from beneath the gardens. The particle is short, but it turns the flowing from a loose image into a source phrase: the water issues from the hidden lower side of the garden landscape. The nasal sound also binds tightly into the following locative phrase, keeping source and under-space compact.

topics.headline: origin from beneath
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rivers are sourced from beneath the gardens, not merely associated with them.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the locative complement as the source complement of the flowing verb.

topics.headline: compact source link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels how a brief particle tightly attaches the flowing action to its hidden source.
topics.reason: The compact prepositional form and immediate complement support the local source-link payoff.

words.gloss_range: genitive locative noun with feminine suffix referring to the gardens; concrete under-space is selected
words.root_gloss_range: under, lower side, and subordinate position; the local phrase selects spatial beneathness with a sustaining underside image
words.prose: {{ar:تَحْتِهَا}} ({{tr:tahtiha}}) fixes the source of the flowing in the gardens' underside. The suffix routes back to the garden noun, and the locative noun makes the under-space concrete rather than a vague adverb. The payoff is not abstract lowness: the scene has a hidden sustaining dimension under the inhabited reward space.

topics.headline: governed garden underside
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the under-space as grammatically governed and tied back to the gardens.
topics.reason: The word is genitive after the source preposition and carries a feminine suffix whose antecedent is the garden noun.

topics.headline: hidden sustaining underside
topics.reader_payoff: The reader pictures the gardens as sustained from below, while abstract lowness stays outside the local sense.
topics.reason: The local source phrase selects concrete spatial beneathness; the sustaining underside image is a valid local enrichment, not a separate abstract branch.

topics.headline: locked paradise-flow partner
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the beneath term as part of the fixed paradise-flow cluster and a surah-local bridge to pledge imagery.
topics.reason: The contextual rows connect the beneath root to its paradise-flow partners and to a later reward-landscape setting.

topics.headline: locative noun with suffix
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that location and reference are compressed into one form.
topics.reason: The locative noun and attached suffix jointly carry the under-space and its garden antecedent.

words.gloss_range: definite nominative plural subject of the flowing verb, the known rivers of the paradise formula
words.root_gloss_range: river, channel, and related brightness or cutting branches; the local plural selects channeled abundant rivers
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ}} ({{tr:al-anharu}}) supplies the explicit subject of the flowing verb. Its definiteness makes the rivers a recognizable component of the paradise formula, and the broken plural gathers many channels under one subject. The root image contributes channeled, force-cut flow; other branches such as daytime or slaughter are only background possibilities, not local senses.

topics.headline: definite river subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the rivers as the explicit nominative subject and a known formula component.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the noun as nominative subject of the flowing verb.

topics.headline: channeled abundant flow
topics.reader_payoff: The reader pictures forceful channeled rivers, while non-river branches are not activated locally.
topics.reason: The local noun and flowing predicate select rivers and channelled abundance; the polysemy row is retained only as a range boundary.

topics.headline: garden-flow square completed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the plural rivers as completing the garden, flowing, beneath formula cluster.
topics.reason: The definite plural form and co-occurrence evidence present the rivers as the final component of the local paradise-flow cluster.

topics.headline: surah return and sound thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the river term as both a recurring formula element and part of the sound-threaded flow phrase.
topics.reason: The later formula return and phonetic row preserve a local recurrence and cadence payoff.

words.gloss_range: masculine plural active participle functioning as circumstantial accusative for the admitted believer group
words.root_gloss_range: remaining, abiding, enduring, and unfading permanence; the local participle selects abiding permanence in the gardens
words.prose: {{ar:خَٰلِدِينَ}} ({{tr:khalidina}}) states the believers' condition as they are admitted: they enter while abiding. The accusative circumstantial form turns permanence into the state accompanying entry, and the active participle makes that permanence a standing condition rather than a passing event. The masculine plural gathers the paired believer groups, while the root stabilizes the moving river scene with enduring residence.

topics.headline: abiding as entry state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that permanence is the believers' state upon entry, not merely a later duration note.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the word as an accusative circumstantial describing the believer group.

topics.headline: mixed believer group gathered
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the masculine plural participle gathering both believer groups named earlier.
topics.reason: The masculine plural form resolves the mixed gender-paired antecedent as a collective circumstantial description.

topics.headline: permanence stabilizes motion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the moving garden scene settle into enduring residence.
topics.reason: The permanence root and garden-river collocation support abiding duration as a core local payoff.

topics.headline: cadence before second purpose
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears an abiding beat before the verse turns to expiation, while the same root's use for other afterlife states does not change this reward context.
topics.reason: The root can describe permanence in other destinations, but local garden admission gives it positive reward value; the cadence row adds local sequencing.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus feminine suffix locating abiding inside the gardens
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهَا}} ({{tr:fiha}}) seals the duration phrase by locating the abiding inside the gardens. The suffix points back to the garden destination, and the preposition gives containment rather than vague association. In one compact word, reference and enclosure are joined before the ayah turns to the second purpose verb.

topics.headline: abiding inside gardens
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees abiding as located inside the bounded garden space, not merely near it.
topics.reason: The preposition and suffix locate the circumstantial abiding within the gardens.

topics.headline: compact locative closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the abiding phrase close compactly before the verse resumes with expiation.
topics.reason: The fused preposition-plus-suffix form compresses containment and reference at the tail of the first purpose clause.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction attaching the second subjunctive purpose operation
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) resumes after the locative duration beat and attaches the second divine operation under the same purpose frame. It does not make admission collapse into expiation or require a strict time sequence; it keeps two coordinated purposes side by side: bringing believers in and removing misdeeds from them.

topics.headline: second purpose coordinated
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that expiation is a coordinated purpose alongside admission, not a swallowed sub-detail.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the second subjunctive verb with the first under the same purpose chain.

topics.headline: resumption after cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the verse restart into a new verb after the containment phrase.
topics.reason: The prefixed connector attaches directly to the second purpose verb after the prior phrase's cadence.

words.gloss_range: Form II subjunctive expiation verb: covering/removing misdeeds away from believers under the same purpose frame
words.root_gloss_range: covering, concealing, ingratitude/disbelief, and expiation; the local divine Form II selects intensified covering-away as forgiveness, reversing the root's negative moral branch
words.prose: {{ar:يُكَفِّرَ}} ({{tr:yukaffira}}) gives the second purpose operation: not only are believers admitted, their misdeeds are covered away from them. The Form II shape intensifies the covering into expiation, and the following separation phrase makes removal part of the action. The root's moral range matters here because divine covering reverses the negative branch of disbelief into protective forgiveness.

topics.headline: second subjunctive purpose
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees expiation as governed by the same purpose frame as admission.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence coordinate the verb under the same purpose sequence.

topics.headline: covering with separation phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that expiation is both covering and removal away from the believers.
topics.reason: The verb takes a separation phrase and a possessed misdeed object, while Form II supports intensified expiatory covering.

topics.headline: covering root reversed by divine agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same covering field turn from a negative moral branch into divine protective forgiveness.
topics.reason: The broader root includes negative covering/disbelief, but the local divine Form II and object select expiation rather than disbelief.

topics.headline: expiation formula and contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the expiation promise alongside formulaic parallels and the nearby contrast with disbelieving forms in 48:6 and 48:13.
topics.reason: The contextual rows supply formulaic expiation parallels and a surah-local contrast with the negative root branch.

topics.headline: knowing-wise covering warranted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader links the selective covering of misdeeds to the preceding divine knowing and wisdom.
topics.reason: Boundary evidence relates the expiation action to the prior divine attribute seal, while the near contrast row keeps the moral polarity visible.

words.gloss_range: separation preposition plus masculine plural suffix referring to the believers
words.prose: {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:'anhum}}) makes expiation spatially separative: misdeeds are dealt with away from the believers. The suffix keeps the same plural community in view, and the prepositional phrase stands between the covering verb and the possessed misdeeds. That placement makes removal from the people as visible as the covering of the acts.

topics.headline: removal away from them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees expiation as misdeeds being moved away from the believers, not only covered in place.
topics.reason: The preposition selects separation and mediates between the expiation verb and the possessed misdeed object.

topics.headline: plural referent compressed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same believer group through a compact suffix instead of a repeated noun.
topics.reason: The preposition plus plural suffix preserves the affected group compactly after the gender-paired object phrase.

words.gloss_range: possessed plural misdeeds as the object of expiatory covering
words.root_gloss_range: badness, moral ugliness, shame, exposure, and harmful action; the local plural names the believers' attributable misdeeds
words.prose: {{ar:سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمْ}} ({{tr:sayyi'atihim}}) names the things being covered away: their own plural misdeeds. The possessive suffix makes the acts attributable, while the abstract noun form treats them as a moral category. The root's shame-and-exposure image sharpens the mercy of the previous verb: what is ugly and exposed is covered away from the people to whom it belonged.

topics.headline: their misdeeds as object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that expiation addresses attributable deeds belonging to the believers, not an abstract stain with no owner.
topics.reason: The plural noun with suffix is the object in the expiation construction and is bound to its agents.

topics.headline: ugly exposure covered
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels expiation as covering away morally ugly exposure, not merely deleting a ledger item.
topics.reason: The root rows connect misdeeds with ugliness, shame, and exposure, which fits the local covering-away verb.

topics.headline: moral category in covering field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the plural deeds are treated as a moral category bound to the covering and belief fields.
topics.reason: The noun form and co-occurrence evidence support a moral-category reading inside the local expiation construction.

topics.headline: near recurrence and arresting sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the misdeed term anticipate nearby badness language in 48:6, with the hamza arresting the word's sound.
topics.reason: The rows give a concrete near recurrence and a local sound effect that reinforce the misdeed term.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening the final evaluative coda
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) pivots the ayah from the purpose sequence into the verdict clause. It carries little lexical weight, but structurally it lets the verse stop listing divine operations and begin evaluating the whole arrangement. The boundary row also makes the coda answer the preceding attribute seal with a divine verdict.

topics.headline: pivot into verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from narrated purposes to a final evaluative verdict.
topics.reason: The conjunction introduces the coordinated evaluative clause after the purpose sequence.

topics.headline: light coda launcher
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a minimal connector launch the passage's shift from divine attributes to divine verdict.
topics.reason: The form is a single-letter connector, and the boundary evidence identifies a shift from the previous attribute seal to the verdict clause.

words.gloss_range: perfect copular verb in an evaluative clause, presenting the verdict as settled
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, existence, and placement; the local copular use asserts settled evaluative being in divine reckoning
words.prose: {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kana}}) changes the ayah from doing to judging. As a copular verb, it equates the demonstrative subject with the triumph predicate; as a perfect in divine assessment, it lets the verdict stand as settled rather than merely upcoming. The being root also fits the following divine-perspective phrase: the outcome exists as triumph in God's reckoning.

topics.headline: settled evaluative copula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the outcome grammatically equated with triumph as a settled divine valuation.
topics.reason: The verb functions as the copula of the final evaluative clause, linking the demonstrative subject to the triumph predicate.

topics.headline: being in divine reckoning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses that the verdict is not abstractly floating; it has evaluative existence before God, while broader place-noun branches remain secondary.
topics.reason: The being root supports evaluative existence; the local copular use and following divine-perspective phrase keep placement imagery subordinate.

topics.headline: purpose chain closed as coda
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the clause as the coda to the purpose chain and as part of a local sequence of settled judgments from 48:4 to 48:5.
topics.reason: The coda and recurrence rows show the clause gathering the prior purposes into a passage-level judgment pattern.

topics.headline: slowed verdict cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the verdict slow before the triumph phrase, giving the coda audible weight.
topics.reason: The phonetic row supports a cadence effect, and the timeless-copula row reinforces the evaluative rather than narrative force.

words.gloss_range: definite distant demonstrative subject compressing the prior reward-and-expiation arrangement
words.root_gloss_range: deictic pointing with distance and address elements; the local form points to and elevates the preceding complex
words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhalika}}) gives the verdict a compact subject. Instead of repeating admission, gardens, rivers, abiding, and expiation, the demonstrative gathers the whole prior complex into one pointer before it is named as triumph. Its distance deixis also elevates the summarized outcome: the referent is recoverable and broad, but it is held at a marked rhetorical distance.

topics.headline: prior complex compressed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the entire preceding arrangement become a single evaluable subject.
topics.reason: The demonstrative functions as the subject of the copular clause and points back to the prior content.

topics.headline: near and broader referents live
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can let the pointer gather both the immediate admission-plus-expiation complex and the broader 48:1-5 promise chain, without losing the local coda subject.
topics.reason: The local syntax supplies the immediate referent, while contextual rows license a broader summarizing reach.

topics.headline: distance elevates the outcome
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the outcome pointed to with elevated distance rather than a flat near demonstrative.
topics.reason: The form's distance and address elements support a marked deictic apparatus, not a bare pronoun.

topics.headline: single pointer carries large load
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the pressure placed on one demonstrative to carry the whole verdict subject.
topics.reason: The occurrence row supports the word's concentrated role as the coda's single pointer.

words.gloss_range: construct-like locative/adverbial term placing the verdict in God's perspective and judgment
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, presence, possession, and being with; the local phrase selects divine reckoning while retaining proximity imagery
words.prose: {{ar:عِنْدَ}} ({{tr:'inda}}) inserts the divine perspective before the triumph predicate is heard. The word is completed by the divine name, so the evaluation is not a free human estimate but a verdict located with God. Its nearness and possession range becomes epistemic authority here: the triumph is what counts as triumph in God's presence and reckoning.

topics.headline: divine perspective frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine perspective is inserted before the verdict noun, making God's assessment unavoidable.
topics.reason: The adverbial phrase modifies the copular equation and appears before the triumph predicate.

topics.headline: proximity becomes assessment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses presence and nearness becoming the authority of divine reckoning, not mere spatial geography.
topics.reason: The local divine assessment clause selects reckoning while retaining the proximity image.

topics.headline: assessment bound to divine name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the evaluative locus completed by the divine name rather than left as a loose adverb.
topics.reason: The construct-like adverb is completed by the following genitive divine name and participates in a dense divine-assessment pairing.

topics.headline: uncommon-root jurisdiction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the uncommon-root pressure concentrate the coda on divine jurisdiction.
topics.reason: The audit row is retained as a local prominence signal for the divine-perspective phrase.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name in genitive after the perspective term, fixing the unique evaluator
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine name with supplied derivational associations of worship, devotion, and needful turning; local force is the named divine evaluator
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allahi}}) completes the divine-perspective phrase and fixes the evaluator as the named God, not an unspecified authority. Its proper-name form matters: the triumph is heard under divine jurisdiction before the triumph noun arrives. The supplied name dispute can keep worship and needful turning in the background, but the local grammar uses the genitive proper name to anchor the verdict.

topics.headline: unique divine evaluator
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees triumph validated by the named divine evaluator, not by human reckoning or an unnamed authority.
topics.reason: The proper noun is genitive after the perspective term and completes the phrase that locates the verdict with God.

topics.headline: proper name not common noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps worship and needful turning as background associations while the local form remains the proper divine name.
topics.reason: The supplied derivational dispute is relevant as background pressure, but QAC and local syntax select the proper name in genitive position.

topics.headline: jurisdiction before triumph
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the triumph noun only after divine jurisdiction has already been established.
topics.reason: The genitive divine phrase precedes the triumph predicate and links divine agency to entry, covering, and valuation.

topics.headline: continuous divine agency thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the coda's divine name continuing the repeated divine presence across 48:1-5.
topics.reason: The recurrence rows identify the divine name as a sustained agency thread through the opening passage.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative verbal noun functioning as the predicate of the coda: triumph as escape plus attainment
words.root_gloss_range: triumph, successful escape, reaching safety after danger, and attainment of good; the local predicate gathers expiation and garden-entry into one verdict
words.prose: {{ar:فَوْزًا}} ({{tr:fawzan}}) names what the whole prior arrangement is: triumph. As the predicate of the copular clause, it does not merely label the outcome loosely; it equates admission plus expiation with triumph in divine reckoning. The root's escape-and-attainment image is especially local here: misdeeds are moved away, believers arrive inside gardens, and the double movement becomes the recognized triumph formula.

topics.headline: predicate equates outcome with triumph
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the preceding arrangement grammatically equated with triumph, not merely associated with it.
topics.reason: The accusative verbal noun is the predicate of the copular clause.

topics.headline: escape and attainment gathered
topics.reader_payoff: The reader understands triumph as both escape from danger and arrival at good, matching expiation plus garden-entry.
topics.reason: The root-image rows match the ayah's double movement of misdeeds removed and believers admitted.

topics.headline: magnified triumph formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears an indefinite triumph opened for magnification by the following adjective and plugged into a recognized Quranic formula.
topics.reason: The indefinite accusative noun is qualified by the following adjective and belongs to a recurring triumph collocation.

topics.headline: formula and opening bookend
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect the triumph formula with parallels in 4:73 and 33:71 and with the opening-to-triumph arc from 48:1.
topics.reason: The rows provide concrete formulaic parallels and the 48:1 opening-to-triumph bookend.

topics.headline: semantic hinge of the ayah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the predicate gather divine admission domains, expiation, and the preceding divine character into one verdict word.
topics.reason: The summary and boundary rows identify the word as the coda's semantic hinge for the whole ayah movement.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative qualitative adjective magnifying the triumph predicate
words.root_gloss_range: greatness, magnitude, bone-like structure, and durable weight; the local adjective assigns inherent magnitude to the triumph
words.prose: {{ar:عَظِيمًۭا}} ({{tr:'aziman}}) completes the verdict phrase by magnifying the triumph itself. Its case and indefiniteness bind it to the preceding predicate, not to the divine name or another noun. The root's bone-like structural image makes the greatness durable and weight-bearing, while the final tanwin cadence binds noun and adjective into a recognized closing formula.

topics.headline: adjective locked to triumph
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the magnitude adjective grammatically bound to the triumph predicate.
topics.reason: The adjective matches the predicate in accusative case and indefiniteness.

topics.headline: durable structural greatness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels greatness as durable structural weight, while the local adjective still simply qualifies the triumph.
topics.reason: The root-image rows support structural durability, but local grammar keeps the word as a qualitative adjective of the triumph.

topics.headline: inherent not comparative magnitude
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears inherent magnitude assigned to the triumph rather than a ranking above another success.
topics.reason: The word is a qualitative adjective completing an indefinite predicate phrase, not a comparative form.

topics.headline: formulaic final refrain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the phrase as a fixed eschatological triumph formula, with parallels in 4:73 and 33:71 and a surah-local magnitude refrain.
topics.reason: The contextual rows connect the noun-adjective pair to recurring formulaic and surah-local magnitude patterns.

topics.headline: paired tanwin closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final paired tanwin cadence bind the verdict phrase and answer the preceding closure.
topics.reason: The cadence rows support the final auditory closure and its relation to the surrounding passage endings.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The causative entry, paired believing men and women, gardens, sub-surface rivers, permanence, and success form one spatial-temporal construction.
baseline_models.mechanism: A gender-complete believing cohort is transferred across a boundary into a planted enclosure whose lower plane carries abundant flow; permanence converts arrival into settled residence, and success names rescue joined to acquisition of the good.

activation_trace.role: Literal passage into an interior supplies the boundary-crossing transfer.
Security and trusted repose make the paired believers secured entrants as well as named recipients.
A tree-screened garden supplies the inhabited enclosure into which they pass.
Continuous streaming supplies motion within the otherwise stable destination.
The distinct lower direction places the flow beneath the inhabited layer.
Water channels cut through ground and make the lower flow materially abundant.
Persistence resistant to decay turns entry into durable habitation.
Rescue from harm plus obtaining good names the whole transfer as success.

changed_reading.before: A generic promise of heavenly reward for believers.
changed_reading.after: A designed transfer into an enduring, water-supported habitat where safety, possession of good, and residence are one mechanism.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The second coordinated purpose covers their bad acts, after which the entire outcome is established 'with/at God' as immense success.
baseline_models.mechanism: Admission has a moral operation beside its spatial operation: bad acts are covered until their active claim is neutralized, while divine nearness, judgment, or standing supplies the evaluative court in which the combined outcome is great.

activation_trace.role: The explicit expiatory covering branch supplies neutralization of wrongdoing as if it no longer operated.
Moral ugliness and defect supply what the covering operation acts upon.
Presence, nearness, and rank in judgment supply the divine evaluative standpoint without requiring physical location.
Magnitude and force scale the integrated admission-and-covering result.

changed_reading.before: Gardens are the reward and forgiveness is an appended benefit.
changed_reading.after: Moral neutralization and spatial admission are coordinate operations, and their unity rather than the garden alone is the immense success.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Entry, gardens, covering, and lasting attachment each carry an interiorizing or sheltering branch inside the focus ayah.
baseline_models.mechanism: The verse can be read as nested protection: persons move inward, the garden conceals and shields, bad acts are screened, and the inhabitants adhere to the protected domain. The mechanism is not escape from visibility alone but controlled interiority around vulnerable moral selves.

activation_trace.role: The inward and secret aspect of entry supplies an interior layer beyond mere change of location.
Concealment from sense turns the garden boundary into a screen.
The protective shield branch gives that screen a defensive function.
General covering extends the shelter mechanism to the entrants' harmful record.
Adhesion and settled attachment keep the protected interior from being a temporary refuge.

changed_reading.before: The verse describes relocation to an attractive place.
changed_reading.after: The relocation builds layered, lasting shelter around both the persons and their exposed moral history.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Dense garden growth sits above opened watercourses whose running is paired with permanence.
baseline_models.mechanism: The stable garden is sustained by a moving lower substrate: channels open and widen below, their flow functions as continuing provision, and the vegetation thickens above. Permanence therefore need not mean stasis; it can mean an unbroken support process.

activation_trace.role: Entwined, vigorous vegetation supplies the living upper layer.
Continuing provision converts river motion into recurrent support rather than scenery.
The lower plane locates support beneath what it sustains.
Opening and widening until material can flow supplies the channel-forming process.
Durability makes the moving support process perennial.

changed_reading.before: Eternity freezes an already completed garden scene.
changed_reading.after: Eternity preserves a living infrastructure in which hidden flow continually sustains visible flourishing.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening announced in 48:1 can be the aperture that makes both admission and irrigation possible: a closed threshold widens for entrants while a blocked outlet releases water. This makes the focus success the inhabited consequence of an opening, not merely a prize placed after a victory.

activation_trace.role: A closed thing opening into a widened entrance supplies the enabling threshold for the focus admission.
Water bursting from its outlet supplies the hydraulic side of the same aperture.
Literal entry receives the widened-threshold function in the focus.
Ground-cutting watercourses receive the released-water function.
Rescue and acquisition name what crossing the opened threshold accomplishes.

structural_cues: 48:1 repeats the opening root in verb and cognate object before 48:5 supplies entry and rivers.
The packet orders aperture before admission, while the focus itself locates moving water below the destination.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies opening, entry, and water channels; I supply the arrow that one aperture enables both human passage and water release. A live alternative is that the opening is solely victory or adjudication and only thematically precedes the focus.

changed_reading.before: The announced opening and the promised gardens are successive but independent favors.
changed_reading.after: The opening is a threshold-and-outlet event whose widened access becomes the focus verse's admitted, irrigated habitat.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surrounding forgiveness root emphasizes a cover that protects the offender from an act's effects, while the focus uses an expiatory covering that neutralizes the bad acts themselves. The two covers coexist as person-directed shelter and record-directed cancellation rather than collapsing into a loose synonym pair.

activation_trace.role: A cover that also preserves supplies the protective outer operation around the person.
Covering fault while shielding its bearer from the effect specifies what the protective operation does.
The closing recurrence keeps person-protective forgiveness active at the far edge of the sequence.
The focus branch explicitly makes bad acts as though not done, supplying record-directed neutralization.
The entrants' ugly or defective acts are the material neutralized by the second cover.

structural_cues: The purpose clause of 48:2 uses forgiveness before 48:5 coordinates admission with expiatory covering.
Forgiveness returns in 48:29 beside a great wage, bracketing the focus's covering and great success.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two distinct covering roots and their branches; I assign protection of the bearer to one and neutralization of the record to the other. They may instead be rhetorical variation without a functional division.

changed_reading.before: Forgiveness and expiation are interchangeable labels for pardon.
changed_reading.after: The context activates a two-surface repair: the person is sheltered from consequences while the bad record is rendered non-operative.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately before the focus, tranquility is delivered into the believers' hearts and makes an inner dwelling; the focus then moves those believers into an outer dwelling. The garden can therefore be the spatial completion of a settlement process already begun inwardly.

activation_trace.role: Delivering something downward to its recipient supplies the arrival of tranquility before human admission.
Inhabiting a dwelling converts tranquility from mood into inward settlement.
The heart supplies the interior site in which that first settlement occurs.
Entry externalizes the prior inward settlement as movement into a domain.
The enclosed garden supplies the outer dwelling corresponding to the settled heart.
Adhering to a place completes inward repose as lasting outward residence.

structural_cues: 48:4 places tranquility in hearts directly before 48:5 admits the same named believers into gardens.
The descent-tranquility-heart sequence recurs at 48:18 and 48:26, making inward settlement a repeated contextual process.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies delivered tranquility, hearts, believers, and later admission; I supply the inside-to-outside completion arrow. The live alternative is that tranquility equips action while the garden remains an unrelated later reward.

changed_reading.before: Garden entry begins only when the believers cross into the promised destination.
changed_reading.after: Admission completes a two-stage dwelling: tranquility first inhabits believers inwardly, then believers inhabit the garden outwardly.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah turns badness from a static item into a circuit: harmful construal becomes a surrounding, returning bad turn and terminates in a bad destination. Against that circuit, the focus covering can be read as interruption of the bad acts' capacity to keep circulating back upon their bearers.

activation_trace.role: Bad construal of others supplies the cognitive starting point of the negative circuit.
Rotation and surrounding give the bad turn its returning, enclosing geometry.
The specifically hated reversal or defeat supplies the circuit's adverse outcome.
What harms or grieves repeats across thought, surrounding turn, and destination, binding the circuit together.
Expiatory covering supplies the proposed interruption by making bad acts non-operative.

structural_cues: 48:6 follows immediately and repeats the badness root three times around a circular noun.
The focus assigns covering to believers, while 48:6 depicts unbroken badness returning upon its bearers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated badness and circular return; I infer that focus covering breaks rather than merely hides that circulation. The alternative is a simple contrast between pardon and punishment with no process-level feedback model.

changed_reading.before: Covering removes isolated entries from a moral ledger.
changed_reading.after: Covering disables a feedback loop in which bad construal and bad action otherwise close around the actor as bad outcome.

context_deltas.mechanism: The pledge scene recasts great success as a completed relational transaction: allegiance is exchanged, a preserved covenant is fulfilled without deficit, and the resulting great wage can also carry an image of setting a crooked fracture. The focus outcome thus includes restored covenantal wholeness, not only possession of a reward.

activation_trace.role: A pledge of obedience supplies the binding relational exchange.
Completion without lack supplies the condition under which the exchange reaches wholeness.
A preserved covenant that secures its party supplies the durable bond being fulfilled.
Compensation for action supplies the overt outcome of covenant performance.
Setting a crooked fracture supplies a secondary repair image within that compensated outcome.
Obtaining good and escaping harm lets the focus success receive the covenant-completion mechanism.
The shared magnitude term links great success to the later great wage.

structural_cues: 48:10 moves from pledge through breach or fulfillment to a great wage.
Its 'great wage' formally echoes the focus's 'great success' while changing the outcome noun.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies pledge, covenant, full performance, wage, and the shared adjective; I infer that the later sequence opens the internal mechanics of focus success and that the fracture branch colors moral repair. The wage may instead be a separate reward, and the fracture image may remain only exploratory.

changed_reading.before: Great success is an unstructured prize bestowed after belief.
changed_reading.after: Great success can also be covenant brought to fullness, with moral crookedness reset and faithful relation made whole.

context_deltas.mechanism: What humans cannot yet reach is already encompassed, preserved, and fully held. That activation changes the focus garden from merely future space into a reserved enclosure whose security precedes the entrants' capacity to access it.

activation_trace.role: Protective keeping supplies preservation of the not-yet-accessible outcome.
Complete encompassing in knowledge and possession makes the reservation already secure.
A protective enclosure supplies the form of the held destination.
Entry becomes later access to what is already encompassed and kept.

structural_cues: 48:21 explicitly contrasts present human inability with prior divine encompassing.
The focus uses causative admission rather than autonomous human arrival, matching access controlled by the holder.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies inability and divine encompassing; I read encompassing as reservation that protects an outcome until admission. It may instead denote mastery or exhaustive knowledge without implying a stored destination.

changed_reading.before: The promised garden becomes secure only when its recipients arrive.
changed_reading.after: Its protective perimeter and divine possession are already operative; entry grants access to a good held before humans can reach it.

context_deltas.mechanism: The blocked sanctuary sequence makes non-entry temporarily protective: immediate advance would trample unknown believing men and women and stain the advancing believers, so access is withheld while hidden groups remain intermixed; admission into mercy and eventual separation govern the delay. The focus promise therefore includes ethical sequencing that prevents new bad acts before covering old ones.

activation_trace.role: Diversion and turning away supply the concrete blocked access that must be interpreted.
Confinement and prevention make even the offering an object held short of its destination.
Security attaches to the concealed male and female believers whose protection justifies delayed access.
A foot physically treading a place supplies the accidental bodily harm the delay prevents.
Being smeared with evil supplies the moral contamination that would rebound from unknowing harm.
Repeated causative entry relocates the admission mechanism from gardens to mercy.
Tender mercy supplies the receiving domain into which protected persons are admitted.
Differentiation and separation supply the unrealized condition under which distinct treatment could proceed.
The focus covering of bad acts becomes the remedial counterpart to contextually preventing a fresh stain.

structural_cues: 48:25 repeats the focus's paired believing men and women and its causative entry construction.
Blocked approach, unknown intermixture, accidental treading, moral stain, entry into mercy, and hypothetical separation form one counterfactual chain.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies every node of the counterfactual chain; I supply the arrow that temporary non-entry is protective mercy and that prevention complements later covering. A live alternative is a one-time strategic restraint that should not generalize to the focus promise's mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Divine admission is best understood as immediate removal of barriers, with covering available after failure.
changed_reading.after: Merciful admission may require a controlled delay that protects hidden believers and prevents the entrants from acquiring the very stain the focus promises to cover.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later realized vision gives focus admission an embodied passage grammar: a promise is made true, entrants cross a barred threshold in security, carry visible completion marks, lack anticipatory fear, and receive a nearer opening. Great success can therefore include an assured but delayed safe crossing, not only the state after arrival.

activation_trace.role: Realizing a promise in action supplies assurance that delayed entry will become actual passage.
The same literal entry branch relocates the focus mechanism into a concrete sanctuary crossing.
Security and heart-rest specify the condition under which the crossing occurs.
Removal of hair supplies one visible bodily mark of completed rite after access.
Shortening rather than full removal supplies the coexisting alternative completion mark.
Expected-harm fear, explicitly negated, defines safe passage as more than physical access.
A nearer widened entrance supplies an intermediate opening on the way to promised entry.
The success/wilderness branch lets the focus outcome include surviving the dangerous interval before safe arrival.

structural_cues: 48:27 sequences verified vision, emphatic future entry, security, bodily rite, negated fear, and a near opening.
The entry and security roots directly recur from the focus while the earlier physical access has remained delayed.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the passage sequence and repeated roots; I infer that it is a concrete analogue that opens the process inside focus success. The alternative is that sanctuary entry is a separate historical sign and garden entry remains wholly eschatological.

changed_reading.before: Success begins once believers are already inside the final destination.
changed_reading.after: Success also inhabits the assured crossing itself: delay, opened access, bodily completion, and freedom from expected harm are part of admission.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing crop simile activates the focus garden's dense-growth branch and reverses the usual subject-object relation: believers are not only admitted into cultivated enclosure; as offshoots emerge, mutually reinforce, thicken, and stand on their stalks, the believing collective can itself become garden-like shelter and support. Destination and cultivated community can coexist without being identified.

activation_trace.role: Cultivation and growth supply the explicit organic process applied to the community.
Emergence from concealment supplies the transition from latent member to visible growth.
Offshoots arising around an original stalk supply plural expansion around a source.
Plants strengthening through mutual support supplies the causal link from plurality to resilience.
A body thickening after thinness supplies maturation into protective density.
Rising and stabilizing on support supplies achieved collective posture.
The supporting stalk supplies the load-bearing structure of the mature stand.
Dense, forceful plant growth anchors the community analogy back in the focus garden rather than letting it become an independent theme.
The believing cohort supplies the same human material that the closing simile cultivates.

structural_cues: 48:29 explicitly likens the community to a crop through a full emergence-support-thickening-standing sequence.
The crop sequence closes with belief, good work, forgiveness, and great wage, echoing the focus cohort, covering, and immense outcome.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an explicit community-crop simile and the focus supplies garden growth; I extend the analogy so cultivated believers can generate garden-like shelter for one another. The live alternative keeps the crop solely as a community portrait and the garden solely as their destination.

changed_reading.before: Believers are passive recipients placed inside an already complete garden.
changed_reading.after: Alongside that destination reading, believers can appear as cultivated participants whose emergence and mutual support produce a dense, stable, garden-like collective.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the success root's desert branch holds rescue and lethal waterlessness together, but it remains anchored in the focus's own success, rivers, protective garden, and entry. Render it only as a paradoxical crossing image, not as a replacement meaning for success or a claim that the garden is a desert.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus places success after entry into a shielded garden with abundant water, allowing the dangerous-crossing branch to illuminate what has been escaped.

activation_trace.role: A wilderness poised between rescue and destruction supplies the hazardous interval inside the success image.
Abundant flowing water supplies the precise material reversal of a waterless crossing.
A protective shield supplies refuge at the far side of exposure.
Crossing inward supplies the endpoint of the hazardous passage.

changed_reading.before: Success is simply possession of the promised good.
changed_reading.after: Success can retain the memory of a lethal, waterless exposure crossed into flowing water and protection.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This activation is branch-distant twice over: the focus entry branch concerns thirsty camels returned to water, and the context dream root resolves non-dominantly to a watering root. It is still packet-licensed and anchored by entry plus rivers, but downstream prose should call it a material analogy and must never translate either the focus entry or the vision as watering.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus causative entry stands beside rivers, while the later vision predicts secure entry and carries a packet-supplied split mapping to quenching and water conveyance.

activation_trace.role: Returning thirsty camels to a trough supplies the strange image of remedial or renewed admission to water.
The actual abundant watercourses keep the watering analogy visibly attached to the focus.
The split mapped branch of quenching rather than thirst makes the promised vision water-saturated at an exploratory level.
Bringing and carrying water supplies a conduit between the vision of entry and the focus rivers.
The later secure entry prevents the water image from floating free of the repeated admission construction.

changed_reading.before: Admission is a single juridical transfer into reward.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, admission resembles being brought again to sufficient water after deprivation, with the later vision carrying that replenishment forward.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The womb-like model is surprising and cross-domain, yet it is doubly anchored by the focus garden root's fetus-in-belly branch and the later mercy root's womb branch, with concealed believers awaiting safe differentiation. It should be rendered as a gestational enclosure analogy only, never as literal rebirth doctrine or as an exhaustive account of the garden.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus combines inward entry and a concealing garden; 48:25 repeats entry into mercy while protected believers remain hidden in an undifferentiated population.

activation_trace.role: A fetus concealed in the belly supplies the focus-side gestational enclosure image.
Movement inward anchors the proposed holding phase in the focus construction.
The womb branch supplies a second packet-backed enclosure around admission into mercy.
Eventual separation and differentiation supply the exit condition from protected intermixture.
The concealed believing men and women supply the protected plurality held inside the analogy.

changed_reading.before: The garden is only a finished exterior destination after all differentiation is complete.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, its concealment can also resemble a protected gestational interval that holds vulnerable plurality until safe differentiation and emergence.

strongest_changes: The opening becomes a single threshold-and-outlet mechanism enabling both admission and river flow.
Two covering roots separate protection of persons from neutralization of their harmful record.
Inward tranquility settling in hearts becomes the first phase of outward settlement in gardens.
Blocked access in 48:25 makes delayed non-entry a form of mercy that prevents harm to hidden believers and prevents a new moral stain.
The safe sanctuary entry and mature crop sequences preserve passage and collective cultivation as coexisting readings of the focus promise.
summary.what_was_special: The focus proved unusually productive as an architecture of controlled access: aperture, inward settlement, protective delay, safe crossing, moral covering, hidden water support, and collective plant growth all remained anchored in its entry-garden-flow construction. Split and distant branches added live water-return and gestational images without displacing the primary habitat reading.
remaining_uncertainties: The causal arrows from opening to irrigation, from inner tranquility to outer dwelling, and from covering to interruption of a badness circuit are reader-supplied rather than grammatically stated.
The divine encompassing in 48:21 may indicate mastery or knowledge rather than preservation of a reserved destination.
The covenant fracture-repair branch, desert-crossing branch, split vision-to-watering mapping, and womb analogy require explicit exploratory qualification.
The cultivated-community reading should coexist with, not absorb, the direct reading of gardens as the believers' destination.
The nearness branch of 'عند' may function as rank or judgment rather than relational proximity.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Entry into a protected inner ecology.** `يدخل` anchors د خ ل B001 (entering) and B003 (hidden interior); `جنات` anchors ج ن ن B001 (concealment), B003 (tree-covered garden), and B008 (protective cover). Flowing rivers below add ج ر ي B001 and ن ه ر B001, water cutting and animating the covered ground. `يكفر` activates ك ف ر B009 (effacing sin). I infer that protective entry and effacement enable enduring habitation. The destination reads as a functioning enclosure, not a static reward-scene.
2. **Winning as safe passage through peril.** `فوزًا` anchors ف و ز B001 (winning good and escape) and B003 (the desert passage between escape and peril). The surah’s departures, blocked route, combat possibility, restraint, and eventual entry supply a journey mechanism. I infer that successful passage is the model joining escape from bad consequences to arrival in lasting shelter. The “great winning” reads as completed transit across risk, not acquisition alone.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 48:25 relocates protective entry into mercy amid an intermingled population, and 48:27 restores promised sanctuary entry after delay. The garden-entry now reads as the culmination of guarded passage.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Double enclosure: dwelling and covered fault.** Fixed `جَنَّات` anchors ج ن ن `B003`, "tree-covered garden," with concealment in `B001`; fixed `يُكَفِّرَ` anchors ك ف ر `B009`, covering or effacing sin. Ayah 48:2 has already activated forgiveness as protective covering, and this ayah places entry into a covered habitat beside covering away bad acts. The packet supplies the two coverings; I infer **removal of exposed liability -> admission into protected enclosure**. Garden and forgiveness become coordinated outside-and-inside shelter rather than unrelated rewards.

2. **Success as passage out of peril.** Fixed `فَوْزًا` anchors ف و ز `B003`, "the desert passage between escape and peril," together with `B001`, winning good and escaping. The immediately following 48:6 supplies the adverse destination, while 48:10 later in this window supplies a binding hand-pledge whose breach recoils on the self. These are the packet's danger boundaries; I infer **protected passage through a consequential field -> safe arrival in the enduring interior**. `فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا` reads as an escape trajectory, not a generic success label.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Ayah 48:6 supplied the perilous alternate destination that made ف و ز `B003` read as passage and escape. Ayah 48:10 added a later risk boundary inside the window: the hand-pledge may be fulfilled or unmade against the self.

baseline.text: İnanan erkeklerle inanan kadınları, altlarından ırmaklar akan ve içinde sürekli kalacakları bahçelere koyması ve kötülüklerini onlardan gidermesi için. Bu, Allah katında büyük bir başarıdır.

findings.text: Bahçelere giriş, kötülüklerin örtülmesiyle birlikte, insanın hem dıştan hem içten korunduğu canlı ve süreklilik taşıyan bir barınağa kabul edilmesidir.
Büyük başarı, yalnızca bir ödül edinmek değil, tehlikeli bir alandan korunarak geçip kalıcı güvenliğe ulaşmaktır.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P1: Opened Flow and Cultivated Enclosure
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: An aperture releases directed movement that becomes life-bearing flow and bounded growth.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The opening is not only an achieved result; the lexical network renders it as an outlet whose released flow irrigates an enclosure.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Outlet, Watercourse, and River
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A blocked source opens, follows a low channel, and cuts a running course through the ground.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: water outlet (`quranic:root_001124:B005/m01`); watercourse or valley-tail (`quranic:root_000521:B004/m01`); river cutting the ground (`quranic:root_001559:B001/m01`); widened opening for water to run (`quranic:root_001559:B003/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 48:1 `فتحنا` and `فتحا` (ف ت ح); 48:2 `ذنبك` (ذ ن ب); 48:5 `الأنهار` (ن ه ر).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The opening functions as a hydraulic outlet rather than a static breach. The same scene gives the trailing watercourse a directional role and lets the river complete the opening by carving and widening a path for sustained movement.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P1: Opened Flow and Cultivated Enclosure
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: An aperture releases directed movement that becomes life-bearing flow and bounded growth.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The opening is not only an achieved result; the lexical network renders it as an outlet whose released flow irrigates an enclosure.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Irrigated Ground Becomes an Enclosure
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Flow crosses receptive ground, gathers in a protected garden-space, and produces increase.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: flowing or streaming movement (`quranic:root_000240:B001/m01`); tree-covered garden enclosure (`quranic:root_000266:B003/m01`); soft fertile earth (`quranic:root_000025:B002/m01`); increase and growth (`quranic:root_000657:B001/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 48:5 `تجري` and `جنات` (ج ر ي; ج ن ن); 48:4 `الأرض` and `ليزدادوا` (ء ر ض; ز ي د), with `الأرض` again at 48:7.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The promised garden is the bounded receiving zone of the released flow. Fertile ground, streaming water, and increase form one cultivation process, making the opening productive rather than merely penetrative.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P1: Covering as Shelter and Absolution
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Covering can protect a vulnerable object or suppress the continuing effect of an offense.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Physical shelter and moral absolution are two operations of the same covering mechanism, but they differ in what is covered and what outcome is prevented.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Protective Cover
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A covering encloses, conceals, and shields what lies beneath it.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: protective covering (`quranic:root_001096:B001/m01`); concealment within an enclosure (`quranic:root_000266:B001/m01`); protective shield (`quranic:root_000266:B008/m01`); covering something from view (`quranic:root_001307:B001/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 48:2 `ليغفر` and 48:11 `فاستغفر` (غ ف ر); 48:5 `جنات` (ج ن ن); 48:5 `نكفر` and 48:13 `كفر` (ك ف ر).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Forgiveness is materialized as a cover, while the garden root supplies both concealment and shielding. The scene protects an interior by interposing a layer between it and exposure.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P1: Covering as Shelter and Absolution
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Covering can protect a vulnerable object or suppress the continuing effect of an offense.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Physical shelter and moral absolution are two operations of the same covering mechanism, but they differ in what is covered and what outcome is prevented.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Covered Liability
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: An offense remains identifiable, but its harmful consequence is covered and removed from operation.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: sin or offense (`quranic:root_000521:B001/m01`); covering a sin and protecting its bearer from the effect (`quranic:root_001096:B002/m01`); erasing an offense by covering it (`quranic:root_001307:B009/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 48:2 `ذنبك` and `ليغفر` (ذ ن ب; غ ف ر); 48:5 `نكفر` (ك ف ر).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: This is not the sheltering of an object but the neutralization of liability. The offense supplies the object, forgiveness supplies the protective operation, and expiation names the outcome in which the offense no longer governs the person's standing.

Geçiş yer, zaman veya iş alanında gerçekleşebilir ve kimi kullanımda azar azar ilerleyen bir süreç olarak sunulur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kişinin veya işin görünmeyen iç yüzünü, gizli tutulan bilgiyi ve giysinin bedene bakan iç kenarını aynı içte kalma düzeninde toplar; dalın tarafsız iç yüz vurgusu bu kapsamı karşılar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: İçte veya gizli kalan yan burada kendi başına kötü değildir; kusur, aldatma ve içten bozukluk bir sonraki dalın sınırıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın dalın içte kalan yan anlamını verir; başka dallardaki kalıplaşmış veya bozukluk bildiren kullanımları buraya taşımaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin, işin veya nesnenin dışarıdan görünmeyen, içeride kalan yanı söz konusudur. Bu yan kişinin iç yüzü ve saklı işleri olabileceği gibi giysinin bedene değen iç kenarı da olabilir.

facets.statement: Bir kişi veya işin dışarıdan görünmeyen iç durumu ve saklı yönü anlatılır.
Giysinin bedene bakan iç kenarı, aynı içte kalma ilişkisinin somut bir görünümüdür.
Birine gizli bir işi açmak veya onun saklı iç yüzünü bilmek de bu iç alanla ilişkilidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kanıt, kişi ve işlerin saklı iç yüzünü merkeze alır; gizli bilginin açılmasını ve giysinin bedene bakan kenarını bu içte kalma ilişkisinin soyut ve somut görünümleri olarak birleştirir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Kişinin veya işin görünmeyen iç yüzü ile bir nesnenin bedene ya da merkeze bakan iç yanı birlikte düşünülürken uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Soyut iç yüz ile somut iç kenarı ortak bir ilişkide korur.

contextual_glosses.text: birinin veya bir işin iç yüzü
contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişinin eğilimi, niyeti ya da bir işin dışarıdan görünmeyen gerçek durumu anlatıldığında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kişi veya işin görünmeyen iç durumunu korur.
error_profile.loses: Giysinin bedene bakan somut iç kenarını kapsamaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Söz konusu olan giysinin doğrudan bedene dönük olan kenarıysa tam ve doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Somut iç yan ile bedene yakınlık ilişkisini korur.
error_profile.loses: Kişi ve işlerin saklı iç yüzünü dışarıda bırakır.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: bir işin veya kişinin iç yüzü
saklı tutulan iş veya açılan gizli iç yüz

error_profile.preserves: Başkalarından saklanan bilgi yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Kişi veya işin genel iç yüzünü ve giysinin somut iç kenarını siler.
error_profile.collision: Yalnızca gizli bilgi adı olarak anlaşılabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal giysinin bedene bakan iç kenarı gibi somut bir iç yanı da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal bir şeyin iç yapısını öğrenme ve gizli olanı bilme sürecini daha açık biçimde kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal kişi veya işin görünmeyen iç tarafını anlatabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Soyut iç yüz alanında güçlü biçimde örtüşürler; odak dal somut iç kenara uzanırken komşu dal gizli olanı öğrenme ve bilme yönünde genişler.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal gizli ya da içte kalan şeyin kendisini ve iç konumunu bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal bir şeyi gizleme, gizlice konuşma veya saklı biçimde iletme eylemini bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da başkalarından görünmeyen bilgi ve iç durum alanında buluşur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal bir iç durum veya iç yan adıdır; komşu dal ise gizleme ve gizli iletişim eylemlerini merkez alır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal içte kalan yanı değer yargısı taşımadan anlatabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal içteki şeyin kusur, bozukluk, kuşku veya aldatma niteliği taşımasını gerektirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal görünmeyen veya içeride bulunan bir niteliğe yönelir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: İçte bulunma ortak olsa da odak dal tarafsızdır; komşu dal olumsuz bir kusur ya da bozulmayı zorunlu kılar.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه باطن الأمر والسريرة والدخلة والداخلة، وطرف الإزار الذي يلي الجسد، وما يطلع عليه من مكتوم الأمر.
